program_name: Smart Agriculture is NOT a standalone degree. Its official name on the University of Turin application portal is 'Scienze agrarie (International curriculum in Smart Agriculture)' (apply.unito.it course id 681). The parent degree is the Italian-named 'Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Scienze agrarie', whose official English rendering in the UNITO catalogue is 'AGRICULTURAL SCIENCE', internal degree-programme code [1703M21], unito.it degree id 42799. 'Smart Agriculture' (Italian: 'Smart agriculture') is one of the curricula/tracks inside that degree; the microsite lists the parent degree's tracks as Sustainable Crop Management, Smart Agriculture and International Cooperation (an additional generic/standard track also exists). Run by the Department of Agricultural, Forest and Food Sciences (Dipartimento di Scienze Agrarie, Forestali e Alimentari, DISAFA), School of Agriculture and Veterinary Medicine (Scuola di Agraria e Medicina Veterinaria, SAMEV).
level: master (second-cycle degree / Laurea Magistrale, 'POSTGRADUATE DEGREE' on apply.unito.it). Nominal duration 2 years, 120 ECTS, organised over four semesters. Mode: full-time, but apply.unito.it notes 'For each year of enrollment, students may choose between full-time or part-time status. Tuition fees vary accordingly.' It is a single-university UNITO degree, not an interuniversity/joint degree (a separate optional double-degree mobility agreement with VetAgro Sup, Clermont-Ferrand, France exists for enrolled students, but that is an exchange scheme, not the structure of the degree itself).
teaching_language: Case 2 - an English-taught PATHWAY/CURRICULUM inside an Italian-named, Italian-language degree. NOT a fully English-taught programme. apply.unito.it states the study language as 'combined English/Italian' (JSON feed field: language = 'en~it'). Only 2 of the 4 semesters are taught in English, i.e. approximately 60 of the 120 ECTS. Official breakdown published identically on the DISAFA microsite and on apply.unito.it: 'The curriculum on Smart Agriculture includes 2 semesters taught in English of 30 ECTS each, in the 2nd half of the first academic year and in the 1st half of the second year.' Semester map: Y1S1 (semester 7) - Agricultural politics, Statistics, Renewable energy - ITALIAN; Y1S2 (semester 8) - Decision support tools for crop management - ENGLISH (30 ECTS); Y2S1 (semester 9) - Applying decision support tools for smart agriculture - ENGLISH (30 ECTS); Y2S2 (semester 10) - Thesis and other activities (internships/stages on farms or food enterprises) - ITALIAN/ENGLISH. Practical consequence for an international applicant: the first semester of year 1 is delivered in Italian, so working knowledge of Italian is effectively required to complete the full 120-ECTS degree even though 60 ECTS are in English. The microsite frames the curriculum as 'suitable for both Italian students and foreign students, and in particular for Erasmus students who choose to spend one or two full semesters at the University of Torino, and for students from international study exchange programs' - i.e. it is partly designed as an incoming-exchange window, not only as a full degree track for degree-seeking internationals. [uncertain - the microsite page carrying this semester table shows 'Ultimo aggiornamento: 23/12/2021' (last updated December 2021); the identical text is still reproduced on apply.unito.it, whose record was updated 2026-06-23, so the structure appears current, but the exact per-semester ECTS split for 2026/27 could not be re-verified against a live 2026/27 study plan because www.sa.unito.it and en.unito.it refuse direct fetches.]
campus: Grugliasco (Turin metropolitan area, Piedmont, Italy) - the Grugliasco agro-veterinary campus of the University of Turin, home of DISAFA and the SAMEV school. apply.unito.it lists Institution location 'Italy, Turin' but Study location / Department location 'Italy, Grugliasco'. The Italian microsite sidebar confirms 'Sede didattica: Grugliasco'. The University's legal/administrative seat is Via Verdi 8, 10124 Torino.
degree_class: LM-69 - Scienze e tecnologie agrarie (Agricultural Sciences and Technologies), Italian second-cycle degree class. Confirmed on the DISAFA microsite in the double-degree description: 'Master Degree in Agricultural science (LM-69) from the University of Turin.' UNITO internal degree-programme code: [1703M21]. apply.unito.it course id: 681. unito.it degree id: 42799.
admission_type: Open access (Italian: 'accesso non programmato' / 'accesso libero') - there is NO national numerus clausus, no TOLC, no SAT and no ranked selection call for this degree. However, open access here does NOT mean automatic admission: enrolment is conditional on (a) a Committee check of minimum curricular requirements (requisiti curriculari minimi) and (b) passing a mandatory assessment of 'adequate personal preparation' (accertamento della preparazione personale), which combines a written test and an oral admission interview. Enrolment with formative gaps ('carenze formative') is explicitly NOT allowed. Exact wording on the microsite: 'Il Corso di Laurea Magistrale in Scienze agrarie e ad accesso non programmato.' For non-EU applicants residing abroad a separate quota applies (see academic_requirements): apply.unito.it states 'This degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad. These places are shared among all the curricula of this degree program.' International applicants apply through the Apply@UniTo (DreamApply) portal within one of the University's fixed admission calls, plus - for visa applicants - Universitaly pre-enrolment.
application_deadline_eu: 2026/2027 cycle. For Italian citizens, EU citizens, EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy, the relevant windows for this open-access postgraduate degree are: (1) First admission call - 25 November 2025 to 29 January 2026, open to ALL applicants for postgraduate degree programmes (this window is also the one recorded for this course in the apply.unito.it feed, intake id 51, deadline 2026-01-29); and (2) Fourth admission call, for open-access postgraduate degree programmes only - 25 August 2026 to 8 September 2026, 23:59:59 Central European Time, explicitly 'reserved to Italians, EU and EU equivalents, non-EU citizens legally residing in Italy' (apply.unito.it intake id 48, deadline 2026-09-08). The apply.unito.it course page carries the comment: 'This call is reserved to European applicants and non-EU applicants legally residing in Italy. If you apply without this prerequisite, your application will not be considered.' The Third admission call (1 July - 14 September 2026) does NOT apply here because it covers only degree programmes with a restricted number of places. Note also that some applicants (typically holders of an Italian qualification) are exempt from applying via Apply@UniTo and instead enrol directly through MyUniTo; apply.unito.it advises checking 'the list of students exempt from submitting their application through Apply@UniTo' and writing to internationalstudents@unito.it if unsure. [uncertain - whether an individual EU applicant must use Apply@UniTo or the direct MyUniTo route depends on where the qualification was awarded, and the departmental interview dates for the September window are published separately on the course site, which could not be fetched.]
application_deadline_non_eu: 2026/2027 cycle: 29 January 2026 (First admission call, open 25 November 2025 - 29 January 2026). This is the ONLY 2026/27 window open to non-EU citizens residing abroad / visa applicants for this postgraduate programme - apply.unito.it lists exactly two intakes for academic year 2026/27 on course 681, and the later one (25 August - 8 September 2026) is expressly restricted to Italians, EU/EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy. For reference, the equivalent 2025/26 window closed on 30 January 2025. Visa applicants must additionally complete the Universitaly pre-enrolment procedure; the University indicates 15 July 2026 as the Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline for the 2026/27 intake. The non-refundable €60 application fee must be paid within the deadline of the call. [uncertain - the 15 July 2026 Universitaly date is drawn from en.unito.it search snippets and from apply.unito.it's Italian-language-certificate notice rather than from a directly fetched en.unito.it page (en.unito.it returns 403 to direct fetches); applicants should re-verify it on the Universitaly and en.unito.it pages.]
entry_exam_or_test: No national/standardised entrance exam (no TOLC, no GRE/GMAT, no SAT). Instead there is a mandatory two-part departmental admission assessment. (1) Curricular check: 'A dedicated Committee appointed by the Degree programme Committee will assess curricular requirements and check the educational qualifications presented by each candidate, that have to include a sufficient number of exams in: mathematics, chemistry, physics, biology, crop production and livestock farming.' (2) Assessment of personal preparation: 'The above mentioned Committee will also assess candidate's personal preparation through in-person and web interviews' - i.e. the interview can be held remotely, which matters for overseas applicants. Per the Italian regulation page, the assessment consists of a written test of 50 questions - 10 for each of the five Syllabus subjects, English excluded - passed with at least 25 correct answers out of 50, and IRRESPECTIVE of the written result there is always an oral interview (colloquio orale) that determines the final outcome. The five test subjects are: Agricultural Microbiology; Crop production; Plant Protection; Agricultural engineering; Animal science (a sixth Syllabus item, English comprehension and translation skills, is assessed but is not part of the 50-question test). Sessions are held periodically in rooms open to the public, before at least three lecturers of the Master's programme, with dates announced on the course website. A candidate may sit the admission test at most twice per academic year; a failed candidate may re-present at a later scheduled date. Exemption: graduates of Italian class L-25 with a final mark above 90/110 are deemed to have adequate personal preparation and are exempt from the test. For non-EU students who must also pass the Italian language proficiency check, the personal-preparation assessment takes place during the same interview as the Italian language test, and that interview may also be conducted in English on the same Syllabus subjects. Candidates lacking the curricular requirements may, on the indication of the Course Study Commission, take single courses (singoli insegnamenti) offered by the University and pass the related assessment before being allowed to sit the personal-preparation check. [uncertain - the 50-question / 25-correct structure and the two-attempts-per-year cap come from the Italian 'Requisiti di ammissione' page as archived on 10 April 2026 (page's own last-update stamp: 11/03/2025); the 2026/27 Didactic Regulation could adjust these figures, and the live page could not be fetched directly.]
academic_requirements:
ENTRY QUALIFICATION. A first-cycle degree (bachelor's) obtained after at least 3 years of university education, or a three-year Diploma Universitario, or an equivalent foreign qualification recognised as suitable under Italian law. apply.unito.it: 'You must hold a first-cycle degree (i.e. bachelor's degree) gained after at least 3 years of University education. You will also need to meet specific admission requirements and demonstrate a suitable academic preparation and a solid background.' Enrolment with formative gaps ('carenze formative') is NOT permitted - the requirements must be met in full before enrolment.

MINIMUM CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS (requisiti curriculari minimi). At least 60 CFU/ECTS in basic and/or characterising educational activities of the Italian ministerial table for class L-25 (Scienze e Tecnologie Agrarie) - or class 20 (Scienze e Tecnologie agrarie, agroalimentari e forestali) of the previous ordinamento - or in one or more of the following Italian scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD): AGR/01-04, AGR/07-09, AGR/11-13, AGR/16, AGR/17-20, BIO/03, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, FIS/01-08, ICAR/06, MAT/01-09. Of those 60 CFU, AT LEAST 30 CFU must fall in one or more of: AGR/01-04, AGR/07-09, AGR/11-13, AGR/16, AGR/17-20. In practice this means an agricultural / agronomy / agricultural-technology bachelor's; a purely biological, environmental or engineering bachelor's will normally NOT reach the 30 AGR-sector CFU threshold. Candidates must document this by attaching to the online application a self-certification of the qualification and of the exams taken and, for students coming from another university or department, copies of the syllabi of the courses taken. apply.unito.it summarises the same requirement as 'a sufficient number of exams in: mathematics, chemistry, physics, biology, crop production and livestock farming'.

SUBJECT SYLLABUS ASSESSED. Agricultural Microbiology (biology and physiology of prokaryotic and eukaryotic microorganisms of agricultural interest); Crop production (food and non-food ground crops and fruit trees of great interest for Italian agriculture); Plant Protection (most common plant pests and diseases and basic knowledge of the main pest-control strategies); Agricultural engineering (basic knowledge of agricultural machinery used across farm types and businesses); Animal science (basic knowledge of stock-farming techniques including livestock nutrition); English (comprehension and translation skills).

GPA / MARK THRESHOLD. There is no published minimum GPA for foreign applicants. The only mark threshold in the regulation is an EXEMPTION rule for Italian qualifications: graduates of class L-25 with a final degree mark above 90/110 are automatically considered to have adequate personal preparation and skip the assessment. Everyone else - including all foreign-degree holders - must sit the assessment regardless of grades.

PLACES AND NON-EU QUOTA. The degree is open access, so there is no overall cap on Italian/EU places. For non-EU applicants residing abroad there IS a quota: apply.unito.it 'Territory requirements' states 'This degree program has 50 available places for non-European applicants residing abroad. These places are shared among all the curricula of this degree program.' Note the wording carefully - the 50 places belong to the whole Agricultural Science (Scienze agrarie) master's degree and are SHARED across all its curricula (Sustainable Crop Management, Smart Agriculture, International Cooperation and the standard track); there is no separate quota reserved for Smart Agriculture alone.

DOCUMENT LANGUAGES. 'The entry qualification documents are accepted in the following languages: English / French / Italian / Spanish. If the document is issued in a different language from those listed above, you will have to upload both the original document and its certified translation.'

[uncertain - the 60/30 CFU SSD breakdown and the L-25 >90/110 exemption come from the Italian 'Requisiti di ammissione' page (own last-update stamp 11/03/2025) retrieved via the Internet Archive; the 2026/27 Didactic Regulation may restate them. Also uncertain: exactly how a foreign (non-Italian) transcript is mapped onto Italian SSD codes - this is decided case by case by the Committee and no published conversion table was found.]
language_requirements:
ENGLISH. The Didactic Regulation treats English B2 as a prerequisite that is assumed/required rather than certified: 'Sono date per acquisite ... una capacita di utilizzo fluente, in forma scritta e orale, della lingua inglese, corrispondente almeno al livello B2' - fluent written and oral command of English corresponding to at least CEFR B2 is taken as acquired on entry. The course Syllabus separately lists 'English: comprehension and translation skills in English' among the knowledge areas assessed. Crucially, apply.unito.it does NOT list a mandatory English certificate (IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge) with a minimum score for this course; instead the 'Language requirements' block names both English AND Italian and states: 'Your knowledge of the English and Italian languages will be verified during the admission interview.' So the English check is an oral/interview check, not a certificate threshold - although a certificate can be uploaded as supporting evidence and apply.unito.it's general guidance mentions 'English language certifications' as an example of documents some postgraduate programmes require.

ITALIAN. Italian is a genuine requirement here, not optional, precisely because this is a pathway inside an Italian-taught degree: the first semester (Y1S1) and part of the final semester are delivered in Italian, so roughly half of the 120 ECTS is not available in English. apply.unito.it explicitly lists Italian alongside English under Language requirements and says both will be verified in the admission interview. The Italian regulation adds that non-EU students subject to the Italian language proficiency test have their personal-preparation assessment carried out during that same Italian-language interview, and that the interview may alternatively be conducted in English on the Syllabus subjects.

ITALIAN CERTIFICATE (CLIQ B2) - DOES NOT APPLY AT THIS LEVEL. UNITO's rule is scoped to first-cycle and single-cycle degrees only: 'Non-EU applicants residing abroad (visa applicants) only. For undergraduate or 5-6-year postgraduate degree programs with free admission taught in Italian, an Italian language certificate at least at a B2 level, issued from 2023 onwards under the CLIQ quality system, is required. The certificate must be uploaded on Apply@UniTo and/or Universitaly by July 15, 2026.' Because Smart Agriculture sits inside a 2-year laurea magistrale, this CLIQ certificate obligation is NOT triggered; the Italian check is done by the departmental interview instead. Accepted CLIQ certificates (CELI, CILS, PLIDA, etc.) and the CISIA ITA-L2 test are nonetheless useful supporting evidence.

[uncertain - no numeric certificate threshold (e.g. IELTS 6.0) is published anywhere for this course, so the English standard is enforced only through the interview and the B2 wording of the regulation; and the exact Italian level expected at interview is not quantified in any official document found. Applicants should e-mail the programme coordinator (Prof. Giorgio Borreani, giorgio.borreani@unito.it) or didattica.disafa@unito.it to confirm before applying.]
required_documents:
Submitted through Apply@UniTo (apply.unito.it, DreamApply platform). Course-specific documents (from the apply.unito.it course page): (1) the first-cycle/bachelor's degree certificate plus full transcript of exams taken, sufficient to prove the curricular requirements (a sufficient number of exams in mathematics, chemistry, physics, biology, crop production, livestock farming); (2) for students from another university or department, copies of the syllabi/programmes of the courses taken (the Italian page requires this explicitly as part of documenting the 60/30 CFU); (3) self-certification (autocertificazione) of the qualification and exams for the MyUniTo route.

General Apply@UniTo requirements for ALL postgraduate applicants: (a) the documentation required for your specific foreign education system (secondary and university qualifications); (b) a MOTIVATION LETTER in English or Italian - this is mandatory for postgraduate programmes; (c) 'additional documents required by some specific postgraduate degree programmes (please refer to "Entry qualification", "Language requirements" and "Other requirements" in the degree program description), such as: minimum credit requirements and English language certifications'; (d) optionally, the degree programme syllabus (course description) issued by the foreign institution, with a translation into Italian, English, French or Spanish; (e) payment of the non-refundable €60 application fee within the deadline of the call (the same €60 applies whether you select one or two degree programmes).

Language of documents: 'All documents uploaded in your online application are accepted in Italian, English, French or Spanish. If your documents are issued in a different language, an official translation in one of the above-mentioned languages is also required.' Entry-qualification documents specifically: English / French / Italian / Spanish, otherwise original + certified translation.

After submission: 'we might require you to upload further documents (declaration of value, statement of verification, statement of comparability issued by CIMEA, etc.)', and 'during the enrolment step, the International Students Office might request further documentation in addition to what was presented by applicants during the application step.'

Visa applicants (non-EU residing abroad) additionally complete Universitaly pre-enrolment and the visa file at the competent Italian diplomatic mission.

[uncertain - this is the University-wide postgraduate document list from apply.unito.it plus the course-level entry-qualification note; no Smart-Agriculture-specific document checklist (e.g. whether reference letters or a CV are expected) was found on any official page, and the DISAFA course site could not be fetched live to check for an additional departmental checklist.]
tuition_or_fees_link: https://en.unito.it/studying-unito/tuition-fees/tuition-fees-international-students (main page: https://en.unito.it/studying-unito/tuition-fees ; instalment deadlines: https://en.unito.it/studying-unito/tuition-fees/deadlines-and-amount-instalments ; ISEE-based calculation: https://en.unito.it/studying-unito/tuition-fees/how-get-calculation-contribution-according-isee-financial-situation). - 'Type: POSTGRADUATE DEGREE, full-time'.
- 'Nominal duration: 2 years. For each year of enrollment, students may choose between full-time or part-time status. Tuition fees vary accordingly. (120 ECTS)'.

uncertainty_notes:
1) PATHWAY, NOT A SEPARATE DEGREE - THE MOST IMPORTANT CAVEAT. 'Smart Agriculture' has no independent degree code, no independent admission call, no independent quota and no independent diploma. It is one curriculum inside the Italian-language master's degree 'Scienze agrarie' / 'Agricultural Science' [1703M21], class LM-69. The diploma awarded is the LM-69 Laurea Magistrale in Scienze agrarie. Aggregator sites (e.g. educations.com) market it as 'Master in Smart Agriculture', which overstates its independence.

2) LANGUAGE - ONLY ~50% OF THE DEGREE IS IN ENGLISH. Officially 2 of 4 semesters, 30 ECTS each, i.e. about 60 of 120 ECTS, are taught in English: Y1S2 and Y2S1. Y1S1 (the very first semester a new student attends) is in ITALIAN, and Y2S2 (thesis and other activities) is 'Italian/English'. apply.unito.it therefore classifies the study language as 'combined English/Italian', not English. A student with no Italian would face an Italian-only first semester. This is a de-facto filter for non-Italian-speaking applicants and should be presented prominently to users.

3) MICROSITE CONTENT IS DATED. The DISAFA page carrying the semester/language table shows a last-update date of 23 December 2021. The identical wording is reproduced on the apply.unito.it record updated 23 June 2026, which suggests it is still the operative description, but the 2026/27 study plan (piano di studi / manifesto degli studi) was not directly verifiable. The exact course titles and the precise ECTS distribution for 2026/27 should be re-checked on the live study plan.

4) ACCESS TOOLS AND WHAT COULD NOT BE VERIFIED LIVE. www.sa.unito.it, www.unito.it and en.unito.it all refuse automated requests (network-level refusal / HTTP 403), so the microsite and the Italian regulation page were read through Internet Archive snapshots (20260514202345 and 20260410173949 respectively) and the UNITO catalogue pages only through search snippets. archive.org began returning HTTP 429 during the session, so the en.unito.it language-requirements FAQ and tuition pages could not be retrieved even via the archive. The programme's official Didactic Regulation (regolamento didattico) PDF for 2026/27 was not located. Everything sourced from apply.unito.it (course record, JSON feed, and the three news pages) WAS fetched live and is the most reliable layer of this record.

5) NON-EU APPLICANTS HAVE ONLY ONE WINDOW, AND IT IS EARLY. The single 2026/27 window open to non-EU citizens residing abroad closed on 29 January 2026 (opened 25 November 2025). The later August-September 2026 window is explicitly reserved to Italians, EU/EU-equivalents and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy. Since today is 1 September 2026, a non-EU applicant abroad can no longer apply for 2026/27 and must target the 2027/28 first call (expected around late November 2026 - late January 2027, by analogy with the two previous cycles, but not yet published).

6) THE 50 NON-EU PLACES ARE SHARED. apply.unito.it is explicit that the 50 places for non-European applicants residing abroad belong to the whole Agricultural Science degree and are shared across ALL its curricula. There is no Smart-Agriculture-specific allocation, and no published information on how many of those 50 have historically gone to Smart Agriculture.

7) 'OPEN ACCESS' IS MISLEADING WITHOUT CONTEXT. The degree is legally 'accesso non programmato' (no numerus clausus), but admission still requires passing a curricular check plus a written test (50 questions, pass mark 25/50) and a compulsory oral interview, with a maximum of two attempts per academic year. Only Italian L-25 graduates with a mark above 90/110 are exempt from the assessment; no equivalent exemption is published for foreign degrees.

8) CURRICULAR REQUIREMENTS ARE NARROW. The 30-CFU floor in AGR sectors effectively restricts the applicant pool to agricultural/agronomy bachelor's holders. How a non-Italian transcript is mapped onto Italian SSD codes is decided case by case by the departmental Committee, and no published conversion guidance was found. Applicants from adjacent fields (biology, environmental science, agricultural engineering abroad) should obtain a pre-assessment from the Committee before applying.

9) NO NUMERIC LANGUAGE CERTIFICATE THRESHOLD IS PUBLISHED. For this course, both English and Italian are checked in the admission interview rather than against a certificate score. The regulation's 'at least B2' English wording is a stated prerequisite, not a documented certificate requirement, so it is unclear whether an IELTS/TOEFL report is formally needed at application. The CLIQ Italian B2 certificate obligation demonstrably does NOT apply to 2-year master's degrees, only to first-cycle and 5-6-year single-cycle Italian-taught programmes.

10) FEES FOR 2026/27 NOT YET PUBLISHED. Only the 2025/26 range (€156-€2,800 per year, income-dependent) is confirmed. UNITO states the 2026-2027 contribution rules are being finalised. The GDP-PPP-based reduction route for international students, and its reported 20 November 2026 request deadline, come from search snippets rather than a directly fetched page.
